newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the weeks of Jan. 13, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - International Business Machines Corp's Lotus division is developing a new technology toward solving a major problem for World Wide Web sites - keeping users from leaving. The technology, code-named DataBolts, will be unveiled in two weeks at Lotusphere, PC Week reported Jan. 13.
Lotus is also developing a series of component applications, code-named MadDog, for its Notes groupware and Domino World Wide Web server software.

COMPUTERWORLD - Sun Microsystems Inc is preparing to unveil January 22 its biggest UNIX-based servers to date, with 64 processors based on Sun's 250 megahertz SPARC chips, as well as a high availability storage system, Computerworld reported Jan. 13.

Several PC makers, including Dell Computer Corp and Hewlett-Packard Co confirmed last week that they are quietly reconsidering their warranty policies - a move that would pass more costs to users, Computerworld reported.
